questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How sailors learned to navigate long voyages without sight of land
The medical effects, causes and long history of scurvy and its cures
How vitamin C was first isolated and synthesised in a laboratory
The spread of potatoes across Europe and its effect on famine
questions.explain: It describes scurvy's symptoms and cause, then its history and repeated rediscovery of food cures.

questions.q: How long does it take for symptoms to appear without vitamin C?
options: A few days
At least a month
About a year
Several decades
questions.explain: It takes at least a month of little to no vitamin C in the diet before symptoms occur.

questions.q: What did Jacques Cartier use to save his men in 1536?
options: Spruce beer brewed on board from conifer needles
Lemons and oranges bought from traders in Madagascar
Lime juice that Dutch sailors had carried from the Moluccas
A tea boiled from the needles of the aneda tree
questions.explain: Using local knowledge, he boiled aneda tree needles into a tea that contained vitamin C.

questions.q: What did Captain James Lancaster's experiment in 1601 show?
options: Crews given lemon juice stayed healthier than the untreated ships
Crews given spruce beer recovered faster than those given lemons
Oranges proved more effective than lemons against the disease
Ginger carried on the ships prevented scurvy in all four crews
questions.explain: Only one ship got lemon juice, while the other crews began to contract scurvy, with many dying.

questions.q: Why did John Woodall's advice not change prevailing medical opinion?
options: His book was never published, so apprentice surgeons never saw it
He recommended foods the company's ships could not afford to buy
Sailors on the East India ships refused to eat citrus fruit
He could not explain why it worked, and physicians saw a digestive complaint
questions.explain: Woodall could not explain the reason, and influential physicians still held that scurvy was a digestive complaint.
